chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to perform the ritual bath on the day of Eid until he had prayed. He said: 'If it is still within the time, he must perform the bath and repeat the prayer. And if the time has passed, his prayer is valid.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating recommendation (istihbab), because we have clarified that the ritual bath for the two Eids is a sunnah, not obligatory. Also, we have clarified that whoever misses the Eid prayer is not required to make it up, but it is recommended for him to pray individually, as we have explained.

key_terms.غُسْلَ الْعِيدَيْنِ: the ritual bath for the two Eids

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the Eid ritual bath before or after praying?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *khuff* (excuse) in ritual purity, distinguishing between forgetting the Eid bath while the prayer time remains versus after it has elapsed. The commentary by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan clarifies that since the Eid bath is merely recommended (*mustahabb*), its omission does not invalidate the prayer, aligning with the broader Shia jurisprudence that missed Eid prayers do not require strict makeup (*qada*). This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding voluntary acts of worship and their impact on obligatory prayers.
